texts.full_text: Created in 1997, by a group of entrepreneurs looking to exercise their expertise in leather goods and fashion, Miriade is a company dedicated to the development, production and distribution of handbags, shoes and small leather goods under license agreements with well-known designer brands. Miriade is currently the exclusive licensee for six brands: RoccoBarocco, RB, Krizia Poi, Valentino, Yamamay and Lancetti. Products are exported to 70 countries worldwide and can be found in high-end fashion and leather goods stores, international department stores and airport duty-free shops. In Italy, brands are available in around 1,000 specialized retail shops as well as Italian department stores and airports. Miriade aims to create value through customer satisfaction and support for the creativity of their products’ designers. Continuous efforts are conducted in research and development to pinpoint the most innovative production technology, hottest market trends and newest materials and colors. Since its conception, Miriade has expanded their portfolio to include other goods including silk and wool accessories, gloves, caps and travel and business leather goods. Each season product line is designed with a focus on functionality, quality, style, comfort, durability, safety, innovation and sustainability in mind. Miriade's commitment to excellence extends beyond the products themselves; it also encompasses their approach towards environmental responsibility. After the ship reached the shore, some of its sailors deserted, intending to remain behind around The Range Hills as farmers; the hills were named Coromandel Hills after the ship and its sailors. ## History The original inhabitants of the Clarendon/Coromandel Valley district were the Peramangk Aboriginal people. Evidence of their occupation is sparse but does include physical artefacts and oral history. European settlement in the area dates back to 1839, when the ship Coromandel arrived at Holdfast Bay (now known as Glenelg) from London with 156 settlers. Amongst these settlers were William Colton, who had been appointed Colonial Manager of the South Australian Company and John Chambers, who was a surgeon and later became a member of the South Australian Legislative Council. The first settlement in the area was the property of John Chambers, known as "Batford". He named his property after the town of Batheaston in Somerset, England. The Chambers family held this land for 117 years before selling to the South Australian Government for inclusion in the new Belair National Park. In 1841 the ship Lysander arrived with more settlers, including John Reynell who established a flour mill at the site which is now the Clarendon Weir. ## Geography Coromandel East is located on the eastern edge of the Adelaide Hills and is bounded by the South Eastern Freeway in the north west, Sugarloaf Hill Road in the east and Main South Road in the south. Unfortunately, this dismissive and/or suspicious attitude is as widespread among wrestling fans as non-fans (“bathroom break” is the usual online descriptor for women’s matches). However, it’s a mistake for observers to simply dismiss this as an part of what “pro rasslin’” is all about or an attitude that is simply to be expected among wrestling fans. First of all, this is an issue related to representation of women in any form or medium. Secondly, and more relevantly for the moment, the sexism and misogyny that pervades professional wrestling is something that has been carefully and intentionally constructed by organisations like WWE (World Wrestling Entertainment, formerly WWF). For about as long as it’s been running, WWE has trained its viewers to dismiss women as secondary athletes and performers, to see them as peripheral to the stories being told about male performers, and to fit into that usual dichotomy of “virgin/whore.”. In much mainstream media, this is an ugly undertone. In WWE, it’s open, blatant, and brazen. [https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/house- bill/1865...](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/house- bill/1865/text) This law is specifically focused on allowing the victims of sex trafficking to seek restitution from companies that profit from their enslavement.The concerns raised by the EFF and other organizations regarding the FOSTA (Fight Online Sex Trafficking Act) and the related SESTA (Stop Enabling Sex Traffickers Act) are rooted in the potential broader implications and the impact on online free speech and the ability of online platforms to host user-generated content without the fear of being held liable for the content of their users. While the primary goal of the Act is to combat the online facilitation of sex trafficking and to allow victims to seek justice and restitution, the broader implications of the Act, as the EFF and others argue, is the fear of increased online censorship and the chilling of online speech. The Act amends the Communications Decency Act of 1996, specifically 47 U.S.C. § 230, to allow state and local governments, as well as victims, to sue online platforms and to allow the U.S. Department of Justice to prosecute platforms as well. This change in the law could lead to platforms being more cautious and, as a result, more likely to remove a wider range of content to avoid the risk of being held liable. This could result in the removal of content and the suppression of speech, even content and speech that are not illegal, to avoid the risk of being held liable under the new law. The EFF and other critics are not disputing the importance of the law in the fight against sex trafficking. texts.full_text: emergency departments and clinics at 8 research centers In this study, researchers investigated the impact of medication nonadherence on asthma-related health issues in a specific population: inner-city children with asthma aged 4 to 9 years old. The study involved 1199 participants across eight different research centers, focusing on the relationship between initial nonadherence to asthma medications and subsequent morbidity (health problems) related to asthma. The primary aim was to determine if baseline nonadherence could predict future asthma-related health concerns in this vulnerable demographic. The study utilized a multisite, prospective, longitudinal panel design to collect and analyze data over an extended period, allowing researchers to track changes in asthma morbidity associated with medication adherence or nonadherence. Findings from this research can provide valuable insights into the management of pediatric asthma, particularly among inner-city children, where environmental factors may exacerbate health disparities.
